articles.title: Heavy rains cause flash flooding in north Georgia, forcing water rescues and evacuations
articles.summary: McCAYSVILLE, Ga. — Thunderstorms caused record flooding overnight in twin towns straddling the Georgia-Tennessee border, submerging some buildings to their rooflines on Thursday as emergency responders rescued dozens of people.
articles.body: McCAYSVILLE, Ga. — Thunderstorms caused record flooding overnight in twin towns straddling the Georgia-Tennessee border, submerging some buildings to their rooflines on Thursday as emergency responders rescued dozens of people. The storms dropped heavy rain across a mountainous area causing flooding on the Toccoa River between McCaysville, Georgia, and Copperhill, Tennessee, causing life-threatening flooding on both sides. The Toccoa then flows into the Ocoee River, where the Tennessee Valley Authority was managing water levels due to the high flows at three of its hydroelectric dams. As much as 8 to 10 inches (20 to 25 centimeters) fell overnight between the north Georgia towns of Blue Ridge and Ellijay, and runoff from uncontrolled streams swelled the rivers below, according to the TVA. The Toccoa River reached a record high Thursday morning of 18 feet (5.5 meters), according to a river gauge in Copperhill, where fewer than 500 people live across the waterway from McCaysville, home to about 1,000. Copperhill emergency officials urged people to take shelter in either town’s City Hall. The river was 2 feet (0.6 meters) above the level forecasters consider “catastrophic,” causing flooding that tops bridges and cuts off access to the community. “It’s over the rooftops in several different areas. Right here in our downtown business district it’s about 6-7 feet high,” McCaysville Police Chief Michael Earley told Fox5 Atlanta. “I have one of my police cars that’s floating down the river right now. Don’t know where it’s at, but it’s somewhere down there.” Photos shared with local media showed some buildings submerged up to their rooflines. Local news video footage showed rescue crews in red boats and motorized rafts navigating through deep, rushing water flowing through downtown streets. Earley said more than 30 rescues were conducted overnight. Robert Poole, spokesperson for the Fannin County Emergency Management Agency on the Georgia side, estimated that about 20 people had been rescued, with no reported injuries or deaths. The water had begun receding by late Thursday morning, he said. “The calls have slowed down as far as people stranded that need rescues, so we’re probably going to end up utilizing a helicopter and possibly some drones just to do an aerial survey and see if there’s anybody out there that needs our help,” he said. “Please do not let the rain stopping give you a false sense of security,” the agency said on social media. “Floodwaters remain extremely dangerous, and conditions can continue to worsen even after the rain has stopped.” The flooding also shut down the McCaysville water treatment plant, causing city leaders to issue a boil water advisory. McCaysville’s downtown previously experienced significant flooding in August that caused damage to the police department, post office and several other businesses and residences. Earley said in a statement at the time that the river wasn’t to blame, but rather “major drainage issues” associated with construction on a nearby state highway.

articles.title: Can Iran’s new supreme leader make peace from behind the scenes?
articles.summary: Mojtaba Khamenei’s consultations suggest a new system of decision-making is taking shape.
articles.body:
Iran’s new supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, is exercising power without appearing in public or allowing his voice to be heard. Since succeeding his father in March, he has governed through written statements and decrees, while reports of his meetings with senior officials offer a glimpse into how he exercises power.

The meetings announced in May and August appeared intended primarily to reassure Iranians that their new leader was alive and exercising authority. But a series of four meetings announced within 11 days in October, involving the heads of Iran’s parliament, judiciary and national security establishment, as well as senior military commanders, suggests something more: a new system of decision-making taking shape.

The meetings come as Tehran weighs its options between negotiations and renewed confrontation with the United States and Israel. They also invite comparisons with the consultations that preceded the 2015 nuclear agreement. The question is whether Iran’s new leadership is preparing for a similarly consequential decision, and whether this system is capable of making one.

For nearly 37 years, Ali Khamenei’s rule rested on his direct personal presence: speeches setting red lines, public meetings with commanders, political elites and ordinary Iranians. His son came to power in different circumstances. Injured in the February 28 strike that killed his father, he was advised, according to sources close to him quoted by Reuters, not to appear or release audio recordings for fear of being tracked.

His rule has taken shape through decrees rebuilding institutions, decisions channelled through a narrow circle of trusted officials, and the testimony of others in place of personal appearances.

The October meetings followed appointments to replace military and security commanders killed in the war. In August, Khamenei appointed his military adviser, Mohsen Rezaei, as his representative on the Supreme National Security Council; Rezaei later became its secretary. Six military appointments followed, including Ali Abdollahi as chief of the Armed Forces General Staff, Ahmad Vahidi as commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and Ali Azmaei as IRGC Navy commander. Abdollahi was also instructed to complete the merger of the General Staff with Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters.

The sequence of Khamenei’s reported meetings is revealing. Those announced in May with President Masoud Pezeshkian and Abdollahi, then head of Khatam al-Anbiya, and another with Pezeshkian announced in August, served chiefly to reassure Iranians that the new leader was alive and exercising his duties. October’s meetings appear to have constituted a systematic round of consultations reaching from constitutional institutions to the armed forces.

At his first reported meeting with the military leadership he had reconstituted, announced on October 31, Abdollahi, army commander Amir Hatami and Vahidi reportedly briefed Khamenei on military readiness in the Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz and the Sea of Oman.

Iran thus appears to be moving from reconstruction to operation: activating a decision-making system rather than merely establishing the leader’s presence.

These consultations unfolded alongside intensive mediation, with each stage of internal consultation following an external diplomatic development.

On October 20, Pakistan’s army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, carried a Qatari-Pakistani compromise proposal to Tehran. According to Arab media reports, it envisaged unannounced inspections of nuclear facilities in exchange for Iran receiving the interest on its frozen funds in Qatar. Khamenei’s meeting with Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran’s chief negotiator, was announced the following day.

On October 26, Munir returned with Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman Al Saud and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin. Their discussions produced an understanding that regional security was the responsibility of the region’s own states. Rezaei also announced that Tehran had sent Washington a proposal concerning the Strait of Hormuz with a seven-day deadline. Khamenei’s meeting with Rezaei, who had received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance, was announced the next day.

On October 30, Qatari mediators held 12 hours of talks in Tehran, coordinated with the White House, after US envoy Tom Barrack suggested an initial understanding was close. Khamenei’s meeting with military commanders was announced the following day.

This timing suggests that internal consultation has become the other side of external mediation.

The statements from these meetings carry two parallel, not contradictory, messages. In the meeting with Rezaei, Khamenei insisted on Iran’s conditions for ending the war, escaping the debilitating state of “neither war nor peace” and managing the Strait of Hormuz. In his instructions to the commanders, he demanded immediate retaliation against any threat without geographical limits, an expanded list of US and Israeli targets, and emphasised that Iran would decide when any renewed confrontation ended.

Repeated appeals for unity suggest an awareness of competing views within the political elite over war and negotiations.

Yet the meetings appear to have defined the upper and lower limits of Iran’s choices, rather than settled on a particular course: at one end, rejecting an intolerable continuation of “neither war nor peace”; at the other, preparing to widen the war if attacks resume. Between these limits lie a settlement on Iranian terms, pursued through Ghalibaf, Rezaei and the mediators, or continued mutual pressure while strengthening the domestic front.

The gap remains wide. Washington wants nuclear concessions before negotiations resume; Tehran first wants the naval blockade lifted, frozen assets released and oil exports restored.

Significantly, Khamenei spoke of conditions “set by the country’s officials”, not by himself. The wording distributes responsibility among institutions and preserves room for him to embrace or disown an eventual outcome.

There are echoes here of the lengthy consultations before the nuclear agreement of July 14, 2015.

A secret channel in Muscat opened with Ali Khamenei’s approval. On September 17, 2013, he spoke to IRGC commanders of “heroic flexibility”, reassuring the military before negotiations. In June 2015, he set out his red lines, and in October he issued a letter of conditional approval. Responsibility for the nuclear file passed from the Supreme National Security Council to the Foreign Ministry under Mohammad Javad Zarif, a sign that the political decision had been made.

The resemblance is clear: a supreme leader establishes red lines, delegates negotiations to trusted figures and brings the military into the process before a major shift.

The differences are deeper. The earlier process lasted around two years under sanctions, not war. Today’s consultations were compressed into 11 days amid armed confrontation, a naval blockade and the approaching November 3 US midterm elections.

Ali Khamenei spoke in his own voice; his son speaks through written statements. Diplomats led the earlier negotiations; now two figures with IRGC backgrounds, Ghalibaf and Rezaei, play central roles. Where the earlier backchannel ran through Oman, today mediation involves Qatar and the countries of the Mecca Agreement, signed on August 7.

Above all, “heroic flexibility” was presented to commanders as preparation for an agreement. Today, conditions for a settlement sit alongside an expanded list of military targets.

The deficit of trust has also deepened. If the legacy of 1979 shaped Washington’s view of Tehran, and the US withdrawal from the nuclear agreement in 2018 shaped Tehran’s view of Washington, the wars of June 2025 and February 2026 have added a layer of mistrust that no technical agreement can easily overcome.

The consultations thus resemble those of 2013 in form but not function. Then, they prepared the ground for negotiations; now, they prepare for a choice between negotiation and escalation.

The seven reported meetings suggest that the new Khameneism may be more than an attempt to fill a leadership vacuum. Its decision-making machinery appears to be in place and functioning, even though the supreme leader’s presence can be established only through others.

Yet every announcement intended to dispel doubts produces more of them, without photographs or details of exactly when and where the meetings took place. The legitimacy of decisions remains partly dependent on the legitimacy of the leader’s presence.

Can this system, with its new commanders and parallel messages of compromise and deterrence, make a decision as consequential as the one taken in 2015, when war has raised the political cost of flexibility beyond what a leader who has yet to appear publicly may be able to bear?

The father saw and was seen; the son makes his presence felt through endorsements and influence from behind protective barriers.

articles.title: Russell Brand is being investigated over two new rape complaints, police say
articles.summary: Det Supt Andy Furphy said he hoped other potential victims would gain "courage" and "confidence" from the guilty verdicts.
articles.body:
Warning: Details of rape and sexual assault

Russell Brand is being investigated over rape allegations made by two more women, it can now be reported.

The disgraced comedian has been found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault by a jury of eight men and four women at Southwark Crown Court, following a three-week trial.

More victims are likely to come forward following his conviction, the detective who led the police investigation has said.

Det Supt Andy Furphy, from the Metropolitan Police, said he hoped other women would gain "courage" and "confidence" from the guilty verdicts.

Brand was found not guilty of two counts of rape and one count of attempted indecent assault.

Brand had initially been coy and quiet in police interviews, said Furphy, but became bolder as officers continued to question him.

"As he gets used to something, he becomes more emboldened by it," Furphy said. "You can certainly see that in his offending."

Hundreds of people were interviewed as part of the investigation and officers said several witnesses came forward, some of whom had previously had a sexual relationship with Brand. Katy Perry, the US singer who was married to Brand from 2010 to 2012, was not interviewed.

Brand, 51, who was described in court as "ruthless" and a "sexual predator", was once one of the UK's most high-profile and in-demand entertainers.

Some of the women said they had been left "haunted for years" by what he did to them.

Speaking to the BBC, officers working on the three-year Metropolitan Police investigation described how bringing Brand to justice was not without its challenges.

Allegations about Brand's behaviour first emerged in the media in September 2023.

The Times, Sunday Times and Channel 4's Dispatches programme jointly reported that four women had accused him of rape, sexual assault and emotional abuse - claims he strongly denied.

The investigation into other reports against Brand began soon after the story broke.

"We kind of assumed that people might want to come forward," Furphy said, "and people came forward."

Victim reports were made to forces across the country and the Met set up a dedicated team of officers to lead the investigation, which it called Operation Actinolite. Officers said they have since taken more than 340 witness statements - including from Brand's former employers, his ex-colleagues and associates.

One officer was assigned to read Brand's books, watch his stand-up routines and DVDs and listen to his podcasts to help build the case.

Brand's high profile and the intense media scrutiny around him proved a challenge to officers, said Furphy.

Another complexity for the team was the allegations were all "non-recent". The earliest dated back 27 years. It meant there was no CCTV and no forensic evidence to work with.

Furphy said police had to look for other ways to build their case.

"Can we look at where the victims were at the time? Who did they speak to in the aftermath of it? Did they tell anybody else? What other available material is there for us to review that might lend some weight to it? Just because it's non-recent doesn't mean that we can't solve it at all."

A former friend of Brand's was called to court to give evidence for the prosecution, while a statement from the parents of one of the women was heard.

The entertainer's former personal assistant, who worked closely with Brand, told the jury about his "insane sexual appetite".

Two months after the police investigation began, Brand was interviewed under caution for the first time. He was interviewed on two further occasions in the following months.

In each interview he provided officers with a prepared statement, which said he did not recognise the complainants or recall the alleged incidents and that if any sexual activity had taken place, it would have been consensual. He then answered "no comment" to the officers' questions.

Charges were brought against Brand in early April 2025: one count of rape, one count of oral rape, two charges of sexual assault and one allegation of indecent assault. The final charge would later be changed to attempted indecent assault at his trial.

The charges all related to women who had come forward since the initial Channel 4 documentary.

The following month he appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court, in London. He was swarmed by camera crews, so much so that it took him more than two minutes to walk the short distance to the court door. At a later court hearing he pleaded not guilty to the charges.

Meanwhile, women continued to come forward with more allegations.

In July 2025, Brand was interviewed for a fourth time before being charged with further offences: one count of rape and one count of sexual assault. He also denied those allegations.

And then on 14 October 2026, accompanied by his wife Laura, the actor and comedian entered the glass dock at London's Southwark Crown Court for the start of his trial.

The women each came to court and gave evidence to the jury from behind a screen, with Brand listening from the dock. At times they cried as they gave their evidence.

Furphy believes there may be more women who will now come forward.

"I think it's likely - potentially - that other women will come forward," he said. "They'll probably gain some courage and some confidence from what's happened in the courtroom over the last few weeks."

He credits the women for their bravery during what has been at times a "deeply uncomfortable" process. "They are courageous, determined women and our focus has always been on them, not Russell Brand."

articles.title: School bus driver arrested after dragging 5-year-old caught in door, authorities say
articles.summary: A New York school bus driver was arrested Tuesday after police say a 5-year-old child was dragged along the road when the child’s backpack got caught in the bus door.
articles.body: A New York school bus driver was arrested Tuesday after police say a 5-year-old child was dragged along the road when the child’s backpack got caught in the bus door. Tasha Van Dayne, 37, of Clinton, New York, was charged with second-degree reckless endangerment, a misdemeanor, according to a statement from the Oneida County Sheriff’s Office. The sheriff’s office said that it responded Monday to reports that a 5-year-old was being dragged by a school bus that was driven by Van Dayne. Van Dayne was driving a 2023 full-size IC Bus for Clinton Central School District in Clinton, a central New York town that is roughly 50 miles southeast of Syracuse, according to the sheriff’s office. Authorities said that the incident occurred on Van Dayne’s afternoon route, shortly after she let several children off at a residence. Van Dayne closed the door as the last child exited the bus and the child’s backpack became trapped in the bus doors, the sheriff’s office said. The child was dragged “a distance” before the bus stopped and the child suffered minor injuries, according to authorities. The investigation is ongoing, the sheriff’s office said. Van Dayne did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Clinton Central School District said in a news release on Tuesday that the driver involved in the incident will no longer be driving students without naming Van Dayne. It added that it takes “an incident of this nature extremely seriously.” “While we are relieved that the student did not sustain serious physical injuries, we recognize that this was a frightening and traumatic experience, not only for the student involved, but also for the children who were still on the bus and witnessed what occurred,” the district said. Van Dayne is scheduled to appear in court on Nov. 16.

articles.title: The Met Gala plays it safe with new exhibition theme
articles.summary: Two months after causing public outcry for planning a 2027 Met Gala exhibit centered on John Galliano, the Metropolitan Museum of Art has announced a new theme: Dressing down.
articles.body: Two months after causing public outcry for planning a 2027 Met Gala exhibit centered on John Galliano, the Metropolitan Museum of Art has announced a new theme: Dressing down. Next May, “ExtraOrdinary: Fashion and the Poetics of the Everyday” will explore the artistic craft behind the kind of mundane garments we live our lives in, like jeans and T-shirts. There will also be clothes constructed literally from common materials like paper and plastic, as well as nods to the luxury fashion designers who have embraced or subverted fashions’ timeless staples — such as a leather biker jacket from avant-garde Japanese designer Junya Watanabe, Pierpaolo Piccioli’s puffer coat ball gowns made with Moncler, or the “I can’t believe it’s not denim” Bottega Veneta pieces that first brought Matthieu Blazy acclaim. “The ordinary is never quite as simple as it seems,” The Costume Institute’s lead curator Andrew Bolton said in a press statement. The new exhibition will feature around 230 pieces of clothing, many of which will be sourced internally within the museum’s current collection. Bolton reportedly told journalists he saw this theme as an extension of the thesis explored in this year’s Met Gala exhibit, Costume Art, which focused on the way in which clothes were worn. Referring to the rescinded Galliano show, Bolton said he “didn’t have a plan B.” “It was really important to come up with an exhibition that was just a masterwork show or something that we could do a little bit more easily,” he continued. “I wanted it to be as challenging and as provocative and as beautiful as a John show would have been.” According to the New York Times, Anna Wintour was not part of the selection process for the replacement theme. While an official dress code for the Met Gala’s red carpet is yet to be announced, Bolton said he hoped visitors of the exhibit might choose to wear their own jeans and beloved T-shirts (perhaps unaware it is the de facto choice for most people). But what might fashion’s biggest night of the year look like with a Casual Friday dress code? Maybe something more interesting than the slick, professionally styled circus of the last two decades. After all, the gala initially was once a much more low-key affair. At the last Met Gala in May, model Bhavitha Mandava caused a stir online after she was outfitted in a pair of Chanel jeans and a half-zip many thought to be far too workaday. Turns out she was just 12 months ahead of her time.

articles.title: Namaste Uncle Sam: Nithya Raman poised to become LA Mayor, as America's top two cities get desi touch
articles.summary: TOI correspondent from Washington: Nithya Raman stood before supporters at a downtown Los Angeles brewery in June, struggling to hold back tears.
articles.body: TOI correspondent from Washington: Nithya Raman stood before supporters at a downtown Los Angeles brewery in June, struggling to hold back tears. The early primary election returns had placed her third in the race for mayor, behind incumbent Karen Bass and reality tv personality Spencer Pratt, and it looked like the end of the road for her. She gave what was almost a concession speech. Her father Venkit Raman, an IITian, comforted campaign workers, telling them her full name Nithya Varsha means 'everlasting monsoon,' and her political life would be replenished soon.It came sooner than anyone expected because after all this is the la la land of Hollywood where plot twists are common. And appropriately too enough considering her husband, Vali Chandrasekaran, is a successful television writer and producer whose credits include 30 Rock and Modern Family. A batch of late ballots that came in took Raman past Pratt to second place, and because Bass did not get 50 per cent of the vote, there would be a run-off election in November. Even then, few gave the 45-year old political tyro, with only six years of experience on the City Council, any chance. Raman herself had once supported Bass, and the 73-year old party stalwart had the backing of the Democratic establishment, including endorsements from Kamala Harris, Nancy Pelosi and Governor Gavin Newsom. She had experience, name recognition, and the advantage of incumbency.What Bass could not quite escape was the perception that Los Angeles is broken and she did not have the toolkit to fix it. The devastating January 2025 Palisades wildfire, which killed 12 people and destroyed thousands of homes, became a defining political liability. Bass was abroad when the mishap occurred and her handling of the disaster and recovery became a persistent political liability. Raman’s campaign ignited. She offered herself as the candidate of change, promising better housing, improved public services and more accountable government. An urban planner by training, she could talk about the nuts and bolts of city administration rather than simply deliver ideological sermons. On Tuesday night, her persistence paid off, and although the race has not been officially called, she is ahead by 25,000 votes and looks likely to seal the deal. She invited supporters to join her in a dance on Wednesday, the tears in June now forgotten.Raman's victory is more than an extraordinary personal turnaround. It is another major breakthrough for the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), the left-wing movement that has been steadily challenging the Democratic Party establishment. And for India, it provides an especially striking political subplot: New York and Los Angeles, America's two largest cities, will now be led by mayors of Indian origin, with Zohran Mamdani already in office in New York.What's even more striking: Long before Mamdani and Raman began making their mark in American municipal politics, several prominent Indian nationalists and intellectuals had encountered the country's radical political traditions first hand. Lala Lajpat Rai spent five years in the U.S between 1914 and 1919, establishing the India Home Rule League and publishing the journal Young India in New York. The radical humanist M.N. Roy arrived in the U.S in 1916 as a global itinerant, encountered American radicals and began studying socialism, subsequently moving to Mexico City, where he founded the Communist Party of Mexico in 1919. He later played a foundational role in establishing the Communist Party of India in 1920. B.R. Ambedkar, meanwhile, studied at Columbia University in NYC, encountering some of America's leading liberal and progressive intellectuals, including philosopher John Dewey. And Jayaprakash Narayan spent seven years in America (1922-1929), studying at Berkeley, Iowa, and Wisconsin, where he encountered Marxism and returned to India a committed socialist.All this was at a time socialism was enjoying considerable electoral popularity. In 1912, Socialist Party presidential candidate Eugene Debs won nearly a million votes, then about 6% of the national total. Socialists also held hundreds of municipal offices, including mayoralties. In fact, in the early 1950s Donald Trump’s father Fred Trump clashed with the folk singer Woody Guthrie, an avowed socialist, over racial segregation and housing discrimination in Brooklyn, causing him to write a song -- a scalding takedown of a predatory landlord -- titled “Old Man Trump" who stirred up racial hatred "in the bloodsport of the human heart."How Socialists are storming across American cities:Indeed, even in the modern era, the current upsurge of socialists did not emerge overnight. One of its earliest conspicuous faces was another Indian activist: Kshama Sawant, born in Pune and raised in Mumbai, who won a seat on Seattle's City Council in 2013. A former economics professor and member of Socialist Alternative rather than the DSA, Sawant became a prominent voice for a $15 minimum wage, rent control and taxing the wealthy. Her victory demonstrated that a politician openly identifying with socialism could win in an American city.Bernie Sanders subsequently took the argument national with his presidential campaigns in 2016 and 2020 bringing democratic socialism into mainstream political conversation, particularly among younger Americans frustrated by inequality, expensive healthcare, housing costs and the influence of corporate money. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez's (AOC’s) stunning 2018 primary victory over veteran Democrat Joe Crowley gave the movement another national face. The election of Mamdani as New York mayor in 2025 was an even bigger breakthrough. Mamdani defeated Democratic political heavyweight Andrew Cuomo by campaigning on affordable housing, free bus services, universal childcare and a city government that would work for ordinary people.The movement now has a growing presence in municipal government. Besides Mamdani in New York, democratic socialist or DSA-affiliated mayors include Katie Wilson in Seattle, Janeese Lewis George in Washington DC, Emma Mulvaney-Stanak in Burlington, Robert Cantelmo in Ithaca and Eduardo Martinez in Richmond, California. In the mid-terms, six DSA-endorsed candidates have won seats in the House of Representatives: Darializa Avila Chevalier and Claire Valdez in New York (both backed by Mamdani), Melat Kiros in Colorado, Angela Gonzales-Torres in California, Donavan McKinney in Michigan and Chris Rabb in Pennsylvania. DSA members Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Rashida Tlaib also won re-election.The organisation's own election tracker reported victories across an even wider range of state and local contests, including in Florida, Maryland, Washington, Oregon, Pennsylvania and Vermont. The significance is not simply the number of elected socialists, but their willingness, like in the case of Raman v Bass, to challenge Democratic incumbents and party leadership rather than wait patiently for establishment approval.While their electoral success is undeniable, the jury is still out on their ability to translate ambitious promises of affordable housing, safer streets, better transport and sustainable municipal finances into reality. Governing New York or Seattle or LA is considerably more complicated than winning an election with a catchy slogan. Already, MAGA bros are cranking up right wing fearmongering with Conservative commentators Benny Johnson invoking scenarios of urban 'Armageddon' a favorite Trump theme.For now though the socialists are having their moment in the sun. The MAGA crowd is predicting an apocalypse, the billionaires are checking their property portfolios, and the Democratic establishment is wondering whether it should start taking out membership in the DSA. Raman and Mamdani now have the rather unenviable task of proving that running a city is not quite the same as running against one. In the process, America's urban political landscape is getting a makeover — and this time, the revolution has an Indian accent.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 3 injured in shooting at Des Moines, Iowa, post office, suspect detained: Police
articles.summary: Police in Des Moines, Iowa, said multiple people were injured and a suspect is in custody following a shooting Thursday at a United States Postal Service facility.
articles.body: Police in Des Moines, Iowa, said three people were injured and a suspect is in custody following a shooting Thursday at a United States Postal Service facility. The incident unfolded at the post office at 1165 Second Ave. Multiple law enforcement agencies have responded to the scene. "I’m in contact with the Department of Public Safety regarding a shooting at the Main Post Office in Des Moines. The suspected shooter is in custody and the investigation is ongoing," Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds wrote on X. "We are monitoring the situation and our prayers are with everyone involved. Grateful for the immediate response by law enforcement." "I’m closely monitoring reports of the shooting at the USPS facility in Des Moines," added Rep. Zach Nunn, R-Iowa. "My prayers are with the victims, their families, and everyone impacted by this tragedy. Grateful to the law enforcement officers and first responders on the scene." Des Moines Police Sgt. Paul Parizek told reporters at the scene that "we're secure right now," according to the Des Moines Register. "I didn't see anything that indicated anyone had any life-threatening injuries," Parizek reportedly added. Parizek said officers responded within three minutes. The shooting happened on the second floor of the post office and reports started coming in of shots fired around 9:10 a.m. local time. The motive for the shooting was not immediately clear. The victims are now getting treatment at a hospital, Parizek said. CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP The public is being asked to avoid the area as an investigation is ongoing. articles.title: JACKSON THOMPSON: Spanberger's office refuses to hand over emails on decision to drop women's sports petition
articles.summary: Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger's office invoked executive privilege to withhold all records on the decision to drop girls' sports protections.
articles.body: Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger’s office is withholding every record it located in response to a FOIA request about the decision to quietly abandon a rule-making effort aimed at keeping males out of women’s and girls’ sports. The Democratic governor’s office invoked executive privilege, attorney-client privilege and a state exemption for gubernatorial working papers and correspondence to deny access to the records concerning the withdrawal of an initiative advanced under her Republican predecessor, Glenn Youngkin. "The volume of records being withheld is less than 100 documents, including many duplicates," the office wrote. "The subject matter of the withheld records is correspondence and deliberative materials." SPANBERGER TAPS LGBTQ ACTIVIST WHO FOUGHT GIRLS' BATHROOM PROTECTIONS FOR STATE BOARD "The withheld records are excluded from mandatory disclosure as working papers and correspondence of the Office of the Governor under Section 2.2-3705.7(2), and/or as attorney-client privileged under Section 2.2-3705.1(2)," the office added. "Your request also seeks information protected by executive privilege." The Virginia State Board of Health withdrew a petition that would have introduced protections for girls' sports on July 30. The effort sought restrictions on male participation in organized female athletic teams and competitions, along with access to designated female spaces where women or girls could be undressed. OutKick's original FOIA request sought emails from members of the governor’s office concerning the withdrawal, covering the period from Spanberger taking office through July 30. OutKick subsequently submitted a narrower request seeking emails from employees other than the officials specifically identified in the gubernatorial exemption. That request also produced no records. "In further response to your FOIA request, pursuant to Virginia Code Section 2.2-3704(B)(3), please be advised that, based upon reasonable inquiry within the Office of the Governor, the requested records could not be found or do not exist," the office wrote. The rulemaking began with a petition filed in April 2025 by Réka György, Lily Mullens and Carter Satterfield. The Board of Health approved that petition 14–0 in August 2025. Youngkin’s administration subsequently advanced the notice of intended regulatory action, which cleared gubernatorial review Oct. 28, 2025. It was published Nov. 17, and the public comment period ended Dec. 17. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER The initiative remained at that preliminary stage when it was withdrawn under Spanberger. The formal withdrawal notice, published in the Virginia Register of Regulations Aug. 24, offered a brief explanation. "Upon review of statutory authority, the State Board of Health is not proceeding with this regulatory action," it said. The original agency background document cited Virginia’s public health statutes as the basis for proceeding. However, it also identified the health department’s enforcement authority and capacity as issues to be considered while developing the regulations. Spanberger publicly defended the decision in September in an interview with Radio IQ. "There’s no legal authority to move forward with rulemaking and prior administrations may have tried to create lanes, and we’re not doing that," she said. Virginia law allows the governor’s office to withhold qualifying correspondence and records prepared for designated officials’ personal or deliberative use. The exemption is discretionary unless another law prohibits disclosure. Its reach can include records written by lower-level employees for protected officials, meaning an employee’s job title alone does not determine whether a record must be released. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP State law also requires disclosure of nonexempt portions of records when an exclusion does not cover their entire contents. The office’s response did not describe whether any records or attachments could be released in part.

articles.title: Five armed men loot ornaments worth Rs 4 crore, Rs 10 lakh cash from bank in Giridih
articles.summary: Five armed men looted UCO Bank in Giridih’s Dhanwar Bazaar, taking Rs 3–4 crore in gold and Rs 10 lakh cash; police raids ongoing, one suspect held.
articles.body: Bokaro: Five armed men looted gold jewellery worth Rs 3 crore to Rs 4 crore and Rs 10 lakh in cash in broad daylight from a UCO Bank branch in Giridih’s Dhanwar Bazaar on Thursday. The miscreants held bank staff and customers at gunpoint for 20 minutes before fleeing with the valuables. They also took DVR boxes attached to CCTV with them. The branch is located less than 200 metres from Dhanwar police station.“Raids are underway to arrest the robbers,” Giridih SP Bimal Kumar said. However, police sources claimed one of the miscreants was arrested in Bansidih in Jamua area of the district late in the night.Rahul Kumar Gaur, branch manager, said the men entered the bank around 1:40 pm. Three staffers, a contractual employee and two customers were present. One of them wore a helmet and the rest followed wearing masks. One of them entered Gaur’s office at gunpoint while the others took employees and customers hostage. They threatened people with firearms and forced them to gather at one place inside a room and tied their hands and mouths with plastic tape.“The criminals then targeted the bank locker and collected the gold jewellery and cash kept inside. After the heist, they fled after locking the bank’s main entrance from outside, leaving employees and customers trapped inside. Gold ornaments and jewellery about 3-4 crores and 10 lakh currency has been looted,” said manager Gaur.Mohammad Mehtab, who had visited the bank to deposit Rs 20,000, said the criminals immediately took everyone hostage after entering the premises. They also demanded money from him. When he resisted, the robbers allegedly assaulted him. Those trapped inside raised an alarm. Locals responded and opened the lock.A police team led by Khorimahua SDPO Amarendra Kumar reached the spot and began a probe. articles.title: Photos: Thousands rally in France over rising costs and economic struggles
articles.summary: Trade unions led more than 260 planned protests nationwide, urging government to address economic woes and wage demands.
articles.body:
Tens of thousands of trade union members joined nationwide strikes and demonstrations across France on Thursday, demanding higher wages and backing a growing high school protest movement, in a major show of pressure on President Emmanuel Macron’s government.

After more than a month of recurring rallies over the rising cost of living, major marches were held again in Paris, Lyon, Marseille and other cities, with unions saying about 260 protests were planned nationwide.

Students staged new actions, with about a third of France’s high schools closed or unable to operate due to student blockades or teachers walking off the job.

Public transport services were heavily disrupted, and the Eiffel Tower was shut for the day. Police in the northeastern city of Strasbourg urged residents to exercise “extreme caution” near certain schools amid tensions.

In Paris, the atmosphere at Place de la Republique was largely festive despite a heavy security presence, after earlier protests on October 17 were marred by rioting and looting.

Protesters gathered under trade union banners as hundreds of musicians played brass, string and percussion instruments, accompanied by choirs, turning the square into a noisy, colourful focal point of dissent over France’s mounting economic woes.

images.caption: People take part in a demonstration in Marseille, France. Trade unions called for a nationwide day of protests against government policy. [Guillaume Horcajuelo/EPA]
Labour union representatives attend a demonstration in Paris as part of a nationwide day of strikes and protests over wages. [Sarah Meyssonnier/Reuters]

Unions said about 260 rallies against rising living costs were planned nationwide, with large demonstrations in Paris, Lyon, Marseille and other cities after more than a month of recurring protests. [Denis Balibouse/Reuters]

About a third of France’s high schools were closed or unable to operate, some blocked by students and others affected by teachers walking off the job. Public transport was heavily disrupted and the Eiffel Tower was shut. [Denis Balibouse/Reuters]

Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said 70,000 police officers were being deployed, backed by armoured vehicles, drones and helicopters. Police have faced criticism for injuring protesters with heavy-handed tactics, and several demonstrations have been marred by violence blamed on masked rioters who do not back the unions’ demands. [Stephanie Lecocq/Reuters]

Protesters wearing CGT labour union vests take part in a demonstration in Paris as part of a nationwide day of strikes and protests over wages, the cost of living and public services called by French labour unions, and joined by high school and university students demanding better school conditions, in France. [Abdul Saboor/Reuters]

articles.title: MICHAEL RUIZ: 'Today' segment may explain key Apple Watch detail in Nancy Guthrie ransom note, expert says
articles.summary: A retired detective says Savannah Guthrie's "Today" show Tucson segment may have sparked her abductor's interest in Nancy Guthrie before her kidnapping.
articles.body: A year after "Today" co-host Savannah Guthrie highlighted her hometown roots and introduced viewers to her mother and favorite haunts, the broadcast is drawing new scrutiny over whether it could have helped make Nancy Guthrie a target in her still-unsolved kidnapping. According to several experts who have been following the case, the same segment could have provided information that influenced the kidnapping — or allowed someone to fake inside knowledge afterward. "There's nothing about the house, but you could easily infer that she would still be wearing that watch two months later," said Morgan Wright, the CEO and founder of the National Center for Open and Unsolved Cases and an expert on digital forensics. "And again, it's not an unreasonable assumption to think that elderly people would take their watch off at night." As Fox News Digital has reported previously, investigators were divided over whether the two early ransom notes were authentic and have not publicly identified their sender. NANCY GUTHRIE RANSOM DEMANDS RELEASED BY PIMA COUNTY SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT IN BID TO IDENTIFY SENDER But Savannah Guthrie's prominence, combined with the personal details included in the segment, could also have caught the attention of someone with malicious intent, according to experts. "I think the segment is worth considering as a very possible spark for someone’s interest in Nancy," said Lisa Miller, a retired detective and law enforcement executive at the Colorado Attorney General's Office who has been following the case. "Whether this involved a kidnapping for ransom, someone fixated on Savannah, or another motive, that broadcast could have introduced a potential offender to Nancy and planted the seed of an opportunity." She called the segment's influence on her abductor or abductors "a strong possibility to investigate" while noting the motive remains unclear. "I want to be very clear — none of that places responsibility on Savannah," Miller said. "She shared her love and pride in a strong woman who raised a family, spent part of those years parenting alone and built a successful career." NBC BEEFS UP SECURITY AT 'TODAY' STUDIO AFTER NANCY GUTHRIE KIDNAPPING, INTRUDER INCIDENT Jim Clemente, a retired FBI supervisory special agent and profiler, separately told the "Crime & Justice with Donna Rotunno" podcast that Savannah Guthrie's fame may have caught the perpetrator's attention. "Whether it actually caused I can't say that, but certainly Savannah's popularity and the fact that Nancy was on her shows and and the relationship between them could have caused some sort of, some type of jealousy or some type of feeling that they belonged to this person, and they wanted to get back at her for not feeling the same way," he said. "It's not logical. It's not something you can anticipate. But it could be possible." What the segment revealed — and what it didn't "Until that story, I didn’t even know she was from Tucson," said Bob Krygier, a retired SWAT commander with the Pima County Sheriff's Department, which is headquartered in the city. "I’ve always had a bit of a feeling that there was some connection." I want to be very clear — none of that places responsibility on Savannah. She shared her love and pride in a strong woman who raised a family, spent part of those years parenting alone and built a successful career. It also shows Nancy Guthrie wearing a white Apple Watch NANCY GUTHRIE RANSOM NOTES MAY BE FAKE AS RENOWNED PROFILER SAYS CASE LOOKS MORE LIKE BURGLARY GONE WRONG The watch detail could have been used by whoever wrote the notes, said Wright, the expert on digital forensics — even if they had no connection to the abduction. One of the notes included references to the crime scene that may not have been public at the time they were sent — including details about the location of Guthrie's Apple Watch and the smashed floodlight in her backyard. Fox News Digital first learned about the watch on the morning of Tuesday, Feb. 3. According to authorities, the note had been sent the day before, on Monday, Feb. 2, indicating the sender knew about it before the information began to seep out into the public sphere. But it could also have been a lucky guess, Wright said. "So I believe none of the ransom notes are credible, and that, that information could have been easily obtained from just watching a video," he said. Krygier said public figures should be cautious about what they share online in today's environment. "You need to be careful, but I also don’t think they need to go into a complete shell," he said. "It’s a balance, but being careful is incredibly important." The 'evolved wrench attack' theory Visit Tucson, a local nonprofit created to attract tourists and business to the city, sponsored the segment, which remains visible on YouTube. It featured some of Savannah Guthrie's favorite locations in her hometown — and the Sonoran Desert's iconic saguaro cactuses. "People ask me, 'Where are you from?' I'm always proud when I say, 'Tucson, Arizona,'" Savannah Guthrie said in a segment that aired on Nov. 5, 2025. "I grew up there, went to college there, my mom still lives there and honestly a part of me has really never left." Guthrie was taken from her home in Tucson's Catalina Foothills neighborhood in the early hours of Feb. 1. After she missed a gathering with friends for church, her family discovered she was missing and called police. The FBI and Google teamed up to recover home security video from her missing Nest doorbell camera, which showed a masked intruder wearing gloves and carrying what appears to be a gun on her front porch. But nine months later, his identity remains unknown — as do her whereabouts. WATCH: Nancy Guthrie's abductor may know family, ex-FBI profiler says "From what we know publicly, I see little that would explain Nancy becoming a target apart from her connection to Savannah," Miller told Fox News Digital. "I also have difficulty reconciling her removal from the home with a straightforward burglary gone wrong." Her abduction required planning and a "consequential decision," Miller told Fox News Digital.
